page: Google Cloud Platform n2d-highcpu-4 is an x86_64 architecture server powered by an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 2 physical cores with 2 threads per core. The system is equipped with 4.0 GB of system memory, yielding a memory-to-core ratio of 1.0 GB per vCPU. It does not include local storage or integrated GPUs, and has zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark data indicates strong single-core CPU performance, with stress-ng single-core tests placing in the top 25%. However, multi-core scaling is limited, as evidenced by weak multi-core CPU scores in stress-ng and Geekbench, both falling into the bottom 25%. Memory bandwidth is mixed; uncached large-block read and write operations perform at average levels, but cached small-block reads and overall PassMark memory scores are weak to poor. Single-threaded compression and decompression tasks show average throughput, whereas multi-threaded bzip3 decompression falls into the bottom 10%.

The primary tradeoff of this server configuration is its low memory density of 1.0 GB per vCPU, which restricts its utility for memory-intensive applications. From a cost-efficiency perspective, it offers a dedicated compute profile for workloads that require strong single-core execution without the overhead of large memory allocations. It is best suited for lightweight compute-bound tasks, single-threaded processing, basic web serving, and small-scale text processing workloads that do not demand high memory capacity or intensive multi-threaded scaling.
